title: Choose the visual world — statusline builder
question: Operate surface, no incumbent identity. The roll assigned The Drawing Sheet, already raised by three hands it beat. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Drawing Sheet
options.lineage: dimensioned engineering drawings and PCB silkscreen legend
options.thesis: The builder is a working mechanical drawing of the bar, and the thing being dimensioned is width in columns.
options.viewport: A warm vellum sheet: parts list left, the bar drawn at true size under a live dimension line, detail callout right, title block bottom-right.
options.risk: Drafting chrome slides into skeuomorphic pastiche the moment it reaches for paper texture instead of line weight.

raised.raise: Ghost cells: a dropped tile stays visible as an unlit witness mark, so absence is drawn as deliberately as presence.
Named silhouettes: the six breakpoints are a fixed visible set of states, never an anonymous slider position.
Cut faces: the inspector exposes the tile's measured internals — spans and computed width — instead of only a settings form.
One snap away: every breakpoint stays pre-rendered so scrubbing the width reads as one continuous object.

options.label: The Specimen Sheet
options.lineage: letterpress type specimen books and galley proofs
options.thesis: The bar shown the way a foundry shows a face: one design, set at every measure, down the sheet.
options.viewport: One tall sheet, the same status line set at 28, 40, 80, 120, 160 and 220 columns, each measure labelled in the margin.
options.risk: Where a careful designer lands by default for anything about measure and type — and it reads as a font tool, not a terminal tool.

options.label: Seven-Segment Family
options.thesis: A rigid cell mask where place never moves and only which cells light ever changes.
options.viewport: The bar as a fixed mask of cells, unlit ghosts holding the places tiles would occupy.
options.case: Wins audience identification outright — everyone knows the flashing 12:00. Loses product clarity: the mask has no vocabulary for measurement, breakpoints, or priority order.
options.risk: Reads as retro novelty the moment the grid stops being strict.

options.label: Cracktro Queue
options.thesis: Rank is depth: brightness, letterspacing and drift rate encode priority without printing a number.
options.viewport: Tile rows riding baselines over black, the front plane still and bright, lower priorities receding into drift.
options.case: Native culture for exactly this audience, and depth-as-priority is a real mapping. Loses clarity: 'nothing is ever enclosed' fights an editor whose subject is literally boxes.
options.risk: A tile editor that forbids enclosure cannot draw the pill it is designing.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Two hard sides, each with a running total that must not overflow the tape.
options.viewport: The config as one folded inlay, rows as sides, column counts right-aligned tight against the margin.
options.case: Strongest product clarity of the hand — 'the sides must not overflow the tape' is precisely the row-versus-columns constraint. Loses audience identification: it is nostalgia, not the notation this audience works in.
options.risk: Handwriting cannot carry a monospace preview, so the one thing being designed sits outside the world.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull turns a flat plane into structured volume.
options.viewport: A flat plane gathering into ribs as a single cord is drawn.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cloth has no columns, and developers do not read couture as their working notation.
options.kept: Named transformation states rather than an anonymous slider.
options.risk: A metaphor with no unit of measure.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Cut blocks of weather and assemble buildings that rain from their own walls.
options.viewport: Sectioned cloud blocks stacked with sky-blue voids between them.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a measuring instrument cannot be built from something with no fixed dimension.
options.kept: Cut faces that expose what is inside a part.
options.risk: Atmosphere where the product needs a ruler.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the viewport and the next is one snap away.
options.viewport: A single item filling the frame with a right rail of action glyphs.
options.case: Fuses poorly: one item per viewport destroys the side-by-side comparison the whole editor exists for.
options.kept: Every next state pre-loaded so movement never stalls.
options.risk: Deletes the comparison that is the product.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark three-pane editor this category always ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Palette left, canvas centre, inspector right, one accent colour, familiar on sight.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other config editor, by design.
